Module 6 · 150–190 minutes

Codes as matter

Assumes: stabilizer measurement updates and rank counting (Module 2) · the toric-code Hamiltonian, defect energy, and local indistinguishability (Module 3) · CSS matrices, cleaning, and the small HGP and BB examples (Module 5) · detection events and noisy repeated rounds for the repetition code (Module 1)

Requires: Stabilizer codes and the CSS construction, The toric code: strings, logicals and matter, qLDPC codes: sparse checks, long connections · Enables: Independent application

By the end, you can
  • Distinguish ground-space protection, an energy barrier, and passive thermal memory.
  • Compute small energy landscapes and state the hypotheses connecting confinement to single-shot correction and thermal bottlenecks.
  • Follow a sector-restricted Ising duality and a coherent gauging preparation with outcome corrections.
  • Interpret the known product matrices as gauge constraints and fluxes in code geometry.
  • Distinguish a Floquet code, a monitored entanglement transition, and an NLTS preparation theorem.

The toric code hides information from every small region. Why can a warm environment still make it forget? What must change for the damaging route itself to become difficult?

6.1 · Stabilizer Hamiltonians and topological order

A small window still cannot read the stored qubit.

Recall the toric checks and Hamiltonian. Each SaS_aSa​ is one of the commuting written checks, a product of Pauli operators with coefficient one. The count mmm includes every written check, even dependent ones. With every check satisfied, the ground energy is E0=−mE_0=-mE0​=−m.

For a Pauli error EEE, the syndrome σ(E)\sigma(E)σ(E) lists the checks that anticommute with it. The energy rise ΔE(E)\Delta E(E)ΔE(E) is two per failed check.

Hcode=−∑a=1mSa,E0=−m,ΔE(E)=2∣σ(E)∣.H_{\rm code}=-\sum_{a=1}^{m}S_a,\qquad E_0=-m,\qquad \Delta E(E)=2|\sigma(E)|.Hcode​=−a=1∑m​Sa​,E0​=−m,ΔE(E)=2∣σ(E)∣.
(6.1)Restated from Eq. (3.6)
Derivation · Count failed checks

Count the terms whose signs change when the error acts. A single-edge ZZZ anticommutes with the two stars at its ends. Each of those terms changes from −1-1−1 to +1+1+1, raising the energy by 222. The total rise is 2+2=42+2=42+2=4. The identity fails no checks and costs 000. Only failed checks contribute to the energy rise.

Within the code space, any operator confined to a correctable region acts on every code state as the same number. No measurement inside that region can tell the code states apart.

PPP projects onto the code space; ORO_ROR​ acts in correctable region RRR; c(OR)c(O_R)c(OR​) is scalar.

PORP=c(OR)P.P O_R P=c(O_R)P.POR​P=c(OR​)P.
(6.2)Restated from Eq. (3.24)

A local Pauli has only two possibilities.

Panel a: a ZZZ edge anticommutes with a star, so PZP=0PZP=0PZP=0; identity gives PIP=PPIP=PPIP=P. Linearity gives the scalar action.

To tell these states apart, we must use a probe that leaves the small window.

Let the readout wind around the system.

Panel b fixes the horizontal readout Z‾h=∏xZh(x,0)\overline Z_h=\prod_x Z_{h(x,0)}Zh​=∏x​Zh(x,0)​ at +1+1+1 in both cards. The dashed vertical readout Z‾v=∏yZv(0,y)\overline Z_v=\prod_y Z_{v(0,y)}Zv​=∏y​Zv(0,y)​ gives +1+1+1 in one card and −1-1−1 in the other. Its support leaves every correctable window.

The transverse operator X‾=∏xXv(x,0)\overline X=\prod_x X_{v(x,0)}X=∏x​Xv(x,0)​ shares only v(0,0)v(0,0)v(0,0) with Z‾v\overline Z_vZv​. Their anticommutation means that applying X‾\overline XX exchanges the cards. Measuring X‾\overline XX instead gives either sign with probability 1/21/21/2 in either card. A state-changing operation need not read the label that it changes.

One Ising spin reads the ground-state label.

Measure ZZZ on the first spin in panel c. State 000000000 gives +1+1+1, while 111111111 gives −1-1−1. One local measurement reads the ground-state label. Degeneracy does not imply local indistinguishability.

A phase describes what survives a small local change.

A topological phase is a gapped phase whose protected information and excitation structure cannot be removed by a small local change. Panel d follows that persistence under a weak local perturbation. Module 3’s virtual winding process explains the finite-size splitting. A small splitting does not itself destroy a phase. Arbitrary commuting stabilizers do not guarantee this stability or topological order. Anyons in an exactly solved model and beyond, PDF p. 6 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1016/j.aop.2005.10.005

We can allow the strings to branch.

Panel a shows a closed-loop basis configuration. Panel b permits a junction where three strings meet, each carrying the nontrivial label τ\tauτ. These strings label configurations in a many-body state; they are not Pauli errors applied to that state.

A string net is a network of labeled strings obeying specified local branching and amplitude rules. Branching rules decide which pictures are allowed. Amplitude rules decide how those pictures enter a quantum state. A junction drawing alone does not specify a Hamiltonian or its excitations. String-net condensation: A physical mechanism for topological phases, PDF pp. 12–14 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevB.71.045110

Panels a and b describe input string labels. For panels c through e, choose one Fibonacci anyon species, called τ\tauτ, whose fusion rule has the same two outputs. The doubled bulk model has additional particle species; its two input labels are not its complete excitation list. String-net condensation: A physical mechanism for topological phases, PDF p. 14 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevB.71.045110

Two τ\tauτ labels can combine in either of two ways.

A fusion channel is a possible total excitation type when nearby excitations are combined. In panel c, 111 denotes vacuum and τ\tauτ the chosen anyon species. The symbol ×\times× means combination; +++ lists alternatives. The source-reported rule becomes the following after translating its vacuum label 000 to 111 and its nontrivial label 111 to τ\tauτ. String-net condensation: A physical mechanism for topological phases, PDF p. 14 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevB.71.045110

τ×τ=1+τ.\tau\times\tau=1+\tau.τ×τ=1+τ.
(6.4)Definition

The toric rule e×e=1e\times e=1e×e=1 has only the vacuum output. Here either 111 or τ\tauτ is allowed. The rule supplies neither their amplitudes nor an exchange matrix.

Check the claim

In τ×τ=1+τ\tau\times\tau=1+\tauτ×τ=1+τ, what does the plus sign mean?

Your answer

Keep the total type fixed while changing an internal channel.

Panel d holds four external τ\tauτ labels and a vacuum total fixed. Fuse neighboring pairs first. Both pairs may fuse to 111, giving intermediate labels (1,1)(1,1)(1,1). They may instead both fuse to τ\tauτ, giving (τ,τ)(\tau,\tau)(τ,τ), and then combine through their vacuum channel.

These are two internal fusion states with the same external labels and total type. Measuring only the total cannot distinguish them. By contrast, a pair constrained to a specified total does not retain both alternatives of the fusion rule. Fixing the total and retaining an internal choice are different operations.

An exchange can change the internal fusion state.

Panel e places the exchange over the space bracketed in panel d. A non-Abelian anyon is an excitation whose exchanges can act on a space of fusion states rather than only multiply a state by a phase. Different exchanges can then give noncommuting transformations of that space. Their order matters even when all external labels return to their initial positions. Anyons in an exactly solved model and beyond, PDF p. 4 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1016/j.aop.2005.10.005

The fusion rule alone does not determine these transformations. We also need braiding data. String-net models therefore extend the language of topological matter beyond Pauli stabilizer codes; they are not all Pauli codes.

A rich ground-state structure still leaves a separate question: what happens along a damaging route?

Optional. In the branching picture, the source’s input labels 0,10,10,1 become our vacuum 111 and nontrivial τ\tauτ. The rule permits a junction where three τ\tauτ strings meet and two pair-fusion channels. It does not yet assign an amplitude to a network.

Local rearrangements relate different network drawings. Their amplitude rules must agree when different sequences of rearrangements reach the same configuration. This consistency is additional information beyond a list of allowed junctions. String-net condensation: A physical mechanism for topological phases, PDF pp. 12–14 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevB.71.045110

The double-semion example already showed why amplitude choices matter: a sign attached to closed loops changes the state. Branching requires more such consistency data. Nor should we identify the two input labels with the full excitation spectrum of the resulting doubled bulk theory.

6.2 · Energy barriers and self-correction

The damaging route has a highest point.

Panel a grows the familiar winding ZZZ row on the L=4L=4L=4 torus. Including the empty start, its energies are 0,4,4,4,00,4,4,4,00,4,4,4,0. Closing the row implements a logical operator, even if the chosen ground state is its eigenstate.

The energy barrier is the smallest possible maximum energy cost along an allowed sequence implementing a logical action. Let FtF_tFt​ be the accumulated Pauli error, with F0=IF_0=IF0​=I and final step TTT. Write S\mathcal SS for the stabilizer group. The normalizer N(S)N(\mathcal S)N(S) consists of Paulis commuting with every check. We ignore overall Pauli phases.

Δbar=min⁡F0=I, FT∈N(S)∖SFt+1Ft single-qubit Pauli max⁡tΔE(Ft).\Delta_{\rm bar}=\min_{\substack{F_0=I,\ F_T\in N(\mathcal S)\setminus\mathcal S\\F_{t+1}F_t\text{ single-qubit Pauli}}}\ \max_t\Delta E(F_t).Δbar​=F0​=I, FT​∈N(S)∖SFt+1​Ft​ single-qubit Pauli​min​ tmax​ΔE(Ft​).
(6.5)Definition

The minimum includes both quantum error sectors. The toric route attains 444, and every first nonidentity single-qubit error costs at least 444, so its barrier is 444. The cube analogue instead joins the classical words 000000000000000000000000 and 111111111111111111111111 using bit flips only.

A flipped region leaves a boundary of failed bonds.

Derivation · Count bonds crossing the flipped region

Before any flips, every bond contributes −1-1−1. Flipping one endpoint reverses its sign and raises energy by 222. Flipping both endpoints restores it. Thus only cut edges contribute to ΔE(V)\Delta E(V)ΔE(V). Reaching the all-zero word requires ∣V∣|V|∣V∣ flips; reaching the all-one word requires 8−∣V∣8-|V|8−∣V∣. Their minimum gives wclw_{\rm cl}wcl​.

Count the cut before counting the energy.

Count the failed bonds for panel b’s supports {0}\{0\}{0} and {0,1}\{0,1\}{0,1}. At V={0}V=\{0\}V={0}, bonds 01,02,0401,02,0401,02,04 fail. These 333 failures give ΔE=6\Delta E=6ΔE=6.

At V={0,1}V=\{0,1\}V={0,1}, bond 010101 has both endpoints flipped and heals. Bonds 02,04,13,1502,04,13,1502,04,13,15 remain failed. These 444 failures give ΔE=8\Delta E=8ΔE=8.

A route peak is not yet the smallest route peak.

Panel c compares peaks 242424 and 101010. Every route from weight 000 to 888 visits weight 333, even with backtracking. Three cube vertices have nine incident edge ends. An edge joining two selected vertices uses two of those ends without crossing the cut. The cube has no triangles, so three vertices contain at most two internal edges. At least 9−2(2)=59-2(2)=59−2(2)=5 edges therefore cross the cut. Three consecutive vertices attain five, so every complete route reaches energy at least ten. The compact route attains that peak.

Both models use unit couplings. The periodic L=4L=4L=4 torus starts in any ground state; the finite cube starts all-zero. Choose row/face or compact/dispersed routes, defaulting to row/compact. Prefix controls jjj and qqq count 000–444 edges and 000–888 vertices; both default to 111. Plots show energy above ground versus raw weight. Readouts give failed checks, cube distance, toric class, route peak, and smallest logical-route peak.

Energy counts failed checks. The cube compares classical bit flips; phase errors have no protection in this model. Step counts select supports and do not represent elapsed time.

Which route has the smaller peak?

The toric route adds Z on h(0,1), h(1,1), h(2,1), h(3,1). The compact cube route flips vertices 0,1,3,2,6,7,5,4. Each failed check costs 2. Predict whether the peak depends only on the number of flipped qubits, then compare the two cube orders.

The toric route peaks at 4. The compact cube route peaks at 10, while the dispersed order 0,3,5,6,1,2,4,7 peaks at 24. The same number of flipped spins can cut different numbers of bonds. The smallest cube route peak is 10 because every route crosses a weight-three configuration with at least five failed bonds.

Follow each compact prefix and count its failed checks. Compare the weight-four cube support. Close a toric plaquette instead of a winding row and explain why the identical energy sequence has different logical action.

Model limits

Finite classical cube, not a periodic 3D toric code. No thermal dynamics or decoder performance.

A thermal bath explores many routes, so energy alone is only part of the memory question.

A bath can create a pair and let it wander.

A thermal bath is an environment that exchanges energy through the specified local interactions. A passive memory is stored information protected by its physical dynamics without repeated active error correction.

Panel a prices pair creation at 444. Panel b moves the pair without increasing energy. Panel c branches into alternative histories, and panel d closes a logical route at zero energy. Energy penalties and the number of available histories both matter.

A lifetime claim must hold temperature fixed and specify how decay changes with system size. For the toric model, a weak-coupling Markov bath, whose approximation neglects memory of earlier bath interactions, gives a largest relaxation time bounded independently of size. This is a dynamical result, not a lifetime read from the cartoon. On thermalization in Kitaev's 2D model, PDF p. 1 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1088/1751-8113/42/6/065303

Check the claim

Why is the gap alone insufficient to establish a scalable thermal memory?

Your answer

The failure is not peculiar to this drawing; geometry constrains whole classes of models.

Two-dimensional local stabilizer models face a general obstruction.

Here self-correction is passive memory whose lifetime diverges as size tends to infinity at fixed nonzero temperature under the specified local noise dynamics.

The two-dimensional stabilizer obstruction

For finite-range, bounded-strength commuting Pauli interactions in two spatial dimensions, with bounded local participation, some nontrivial logical route has a size-independent energy barrier. The strip construction confines failed checks near the moving ends. This theorem does not cover every noncommuting two-dimensional Hamiltonian. A no-go theorem for a two-dimensional self-correcting quantum memory based on stabilizer codes, PDF pp. 2–4 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1088/1367-2630/11/4/043029

The equation strip under the figure states the geometric assumptions behind this obstruction; panel a places the 2D toric code. Bounded participation means each qubit enters only a bounded number of terms as size grows.

Check the claim

Which change leaves the stated Bravyi-Terhal theorem outside its assumptions?

Your answer

Changing the dimension changes the boundary of an error.

A membrane can carry a growing loop boundary.

A membrane operator is an operator supported on a two-dimensional sheet of qubits. In panel b, four-dimensional toric qubits occupy faces. Each link XXX check acts on its six incident faces; each cube ZZZ check acts on its six boundary faces. Topological quantum memory, PDF pp. 35–36 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1063/1.1499754

A partial ZZZ sheet fails link checks along its loop boundary. A dual XXX sheet similarly leaves a loop of failed cube checks. Both conjugate sectors therefore acquire extended defect boundaries. Closing a logical membrane removes the boundary and returns to the ground space.

This geometry supplies an energetic mechanism. A separate low-temperature theorem uses weak-coupling Markov dynamics of Davies type to obtain long relaxation times for dressed logical observables. Their readout accounts for local defects; they are not bare membrane products. On thermal stability of topological qubit in Kitaev's 4D model, PDF p. 1 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1142/s1230161210000023

Check the claim

What is the useful change in the 4D toric example?

Your answer

Three dimensions can also obstruct motion, but the result need not be a full thermal memory.

A defect need not have a freely extendable string.

A fracton is a point-like excitation whose motion is constrained so that an isolated defect cannot be freely translated by a thin local operator. Panel c marks the point-like defects of Haah’s Code 1; these point-like defects are fractons.

Haah’s three-dimensional Code 1 forbids freely extendable thin-string transport of an isolated defect. Its local check pattern makes extending a narrow support leave additional failed checks. This is a property of the specified code, not of every model in three dimensions. Local stabilizer codes in three dimensions without string logical operators, PDF pp. 6–8 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevA.83.042330

The intermediate errors can cost more than the final error.

The toric route finishes with zero syndrome but passes through energy 444. Likewise, a completed Haah support does not specify the costs of assembling it. For periodic Code 1 with L=2pL=2^pL=2p, the cited construction matches a logarithmic barrier lower bound with a logarithmic upper bound. This concerns the largest intermediate cost while assembling a logical operator, not its final syndrome. On the energy landscape of 3D spin Hamiltonians with topological order, PDF pp. 5–6 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.107.150504

Check the claim

A completed error has a small final syndrome. What has this shown about its assembly barrier, for the toric route or the cited Haah model?

Your answer

A barrier result still needs a dynamical theorem before it becomes a lifetime claim.

The proved lifetime improvement stops at a temperature-dependent size.

For the cited Haah model with Davies dynamics, the lifetime bound applies only below a maximum size that depends on temperature. Holding a nonzero temperature fixed therefore prevents extrapolating this theorem to arbitrarily large systems. It does not establish self-correction in the infinite-size sense. Analytic and numerical demonstration of quantum self-correction in the 3D Cubic Code, PDF p. 1 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.111.200501

Read the separate barrier label and the hatched finite-size-benefit note in panel c. They answer different questions. Panel d’s graph-local footer changes the interaction assumption: sparse edges need not fit a finite-range spatial lattice. It is not an additional spatial dimension.

The common question is whether a large error can hide behind a small syndrome.

A theory of single-shot error correction for adversarial noise, PDF pp. 3–5 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1088/2058-9565/aafc8f

To extend the cube’s syndrome-growth idea to a quantum family, Quintavalle and colleagues assume linear confinement in same-syndrome reduced weight wsynw_{\rm syn}wsyn​. Its positive slope must stay uniform as size grows. The confinement range must grow at least as a positive power of size. The code distance must also grow at least as a positive power of size. Each qubit may enter only a bounded number of checks. Data and report noise must be local stochastic and sufficiently weak. Here local stochastic means that faults at a specified set of locations become exponentially unlikely as the set grows.

Under these assumptions, one noisy measurement round followed by processing leaves a controlled residual error. Repeating such rounds keeps that residual under control. The failure estimates fall exponentially with the size of the relevant fault sets.

The theorem’s XXX-confinement form protects only ZZZ errors. The cube instead demonstrates bit-flip correction in one finite classical model. It does not establish this growing-family guarantee. Single-shot error correction of three-dimensional homological product codes, PDF pp. 3–4 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1103/PRXQuantum.2.020340

Campbell’s soundness theorem for adversarial noise gives a different promise. Within its limits on data-error and report-error sizes, it covers every pattern, regardless of fault locations. After correction, the stabilizer-reduced residual weight is bounded by a function of the number of wrong reports. This theorem supplies no threshold for random noise rates. It also does not supply an efficient decoder. A theory of single-shot error correction for adversarial noise, PDF pp. 3–5 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1088/2058-9565/aafc8f

Panel a recalls the toric route. Panel b instead groups states into basins connected by local moves. Panel c marks boundary states through which those moves can leave a basin. We sum thermal weights over each set; a single route’s highest energy does not determine either sum.

Many boundary states can offset their individual energy penalties. A small total boundary weight relative to the basin supports slow escape under suitable local dynamics. The relevant thermal state can separate into many long-lived components.

A typical component retains long-range entanglement.

Panel d separates two quantum claims. A typical component cannot be represented as a mixture of states prepared by shallow local circuits. Topological Quantum Spin Glass Order and its realization in qLDPC codes, PDF pp. 3–4, Theorem II.1 Original source ↗

Here ergodicity breaking is dynamics remaining confined to one of many state-space components on a diverging time scale. The term topological quantum spin-glass order is the component structure described by the cited theorem, combining slow motion between components with quantum order within typical components.

Hypotheses behind the component picture

Start with sparse CSS checks, so each check touches few qubits and each qubit participates in few checks. The code family must have a fixed positive rate. No written check may be a product of the others. Both error sectors must have linear confinement measured by the stabilizer-reduced weight. Its slope must exceed a threshold set by the code rate. The confinement range must grow faster than the logarithm of the number of qubits. The temperature must be low enough. Topological Quantum Spin Glass Order and its realization in qLDPC codes, PDF pp. 4–6 Original source ↗

The interactions are local on a bounded-degree graph, with bounded check weights and couplings. They need not be finite-range interactions in Euclidean space. The dynamical statement concerns local evolution preserving the Gibbs state, not an arbitrary bath. Its boundary estimates apply to local quantum channels with that stationary state. Topological Quantum Spin Glass Order and its realization in qLDPC codes, PDF p. 3 Original source ↗

The paper’s syndrome-count energy becomes ΔE=2∣σ∣\Delta E=2|\sigma|ΔE=2∣σ∣ in our convention. This rescales temperature units without changing the component structure. The full Gibbs state remains a thermal mixture, not a pure toric ground state.

The sixteen matter strings each have amplitude 1/41/41/4. For T=∅T=\varnothingT=∅, all links are zero. Adding h(0,0)h(0,0)h(0,0) writes x0⊕x1x_0\oplus x_1x0​⊕x1​ there, leaving the others blank.

Each CNOT pair changes only its link. Induction over TTT gives the sum. At full transfer, all eight bits form DxDxDx. The formula holds before matter measurement.

The signs remember the outcomes, so we must track or correct their byproduct.

Use a link Z to correct the two negative stars.

A measurement byproduct is an outcome-dependent operator or sign that must be tracked or corrected after measurement. A link Z reverses endpoint stars, preserving Z fluxes.

Let the binary edge vector ccc select the correction Z(c)Z(c)Z(c). Its boundary ∂c\partial c∂c marks odd-incidence vertices. Here ∂=DT\partial=D^T∂=DT is vertex-by-edge incidence, transposing the state sum’s matrix.

For 110011001100, choose c={h(0,0)}c=\{h(0,0)\}c={h(0,0)}, joining the first two vertices. For 101010101010, choose c={v(0,0)}c=\{v(0,0)\}c={v(0,0)}, joining the first and third vertices. Both corrections have the required boundary.

The corrected state sums eight cut strings coherently, each with amplitude 1/81/\sqrt81/8​. The logical Z loops h(0,0)+h(1,0)h(0,0)+h(1,0)h(0,0)+h(1,0) and v(0,0)+v(0,1)v(0,0)+v(0,1)v(0,0)+v(0,1) both have sign +1+1+1. Cuts intersect these loops evenly, and Z corrections preserve their signs. This prepares one fixed-sector ground state, with no arbitrary encoded input.

What does the corrected L=2L=2L=2 preparation produce?

Your answer

Stage is a dimensionless operation index. Stage 0 hides blank links; stage 1 reveals them. Stages 2 through 9 transfer successive bond parities. Stages 10 through 13 measure matter in vertex order. Stage 14 corrects and discards matter.

Two CNOTs for one bond constitute one parity-transfer operation in the stepper. They are sequential inside its model function. This is an operation sequence, not a circuit-depth or hardware schedule claim. The source’s cluster-state protocol is globally Hadamard-transformed on links into this course convention.

The outcome control selects an even branch, without forcing its physical outcome. The plot counts coupled bonds against stage. Check readings show expectations; zero means uncertain. The probability readout tracks the branch. This ideal model omits measurement noise and establishes no fault-tolerance guarantee.

What will the matter record leave behind?

Four matter qubits start in |+> and eight links in |0>. Each link receives the XOR of its endpoint bits coherently. After this transfer, every G_v=X_v A_v and every B_p has value +1. Predict the link-star signs after matter X outcomes 1100 in vertex order (0,0),(1,0),(0,1),(1,1). Which link Z can make them all positive?

The star signs are −1,−1,+1,+1. A Z on h(0,0) changes exactly the first two star signs and preserves all fluxes. The record has probability 1/8. The final link state lies in the toric ground space with logical Z signs +1,+1.

Follow the bond parities before reading matter. Inspect the negative star signs from record 1100. Apply the endpoint correction and compare all check readings.

Tangent: what the duality does with a boundary

Optional. The open chain has two independent bonds and a global flip label. The symmetric sector removes that label The Physics of (good) LDPC Codes I. Gauging and dualities, PDF p. 13 Original source ↗.

On a closed NNN-site chain, (Z0Z1)(Z1Z2)⋯(ZN−1Z0)=Z02Z12⋯ZN−12=I(Z_0Z_1)(Z_1Z_2)\cdots(Z_{N-1}Z_0)=Z_0^2Z_1^2\cdots Z_{N-1}^2=I(Z0​Z1​)(Z1​Z2​)⋯(ZN−1​Z0​)=Z02​Z12​⋯ZN−12​=I: every spin occurs twice. Thus the bond variables obey a product constraint.

One negative background gauge sign makes the product negative, representing an antiperiodic twist. The duality must retain this boundary sector The Physics of (good) LDPC Codes I. Gauging and dualities, PDF p. 7 Original source ↗.

Positive star and flux terms, with vanishing matter hopping and electric-field perturbations, give the toric fixed point.

A higher-form symmetry is a conservation rule for extended charged objects. Picture closed field lines and a surface counting their crossings. This global extended symmetry differs from local GvG_vGv​ transformations, which change the description of the same physical state The Physics of (good) LDPC Codes I. The same rows tell us how an excitation moves when an error grows.

Extend an error along an input layer.

Starting in the ground space, Z0Z_0Z0​ fails X row 0 and costs energy 222. Adding Z2Z_2Z2​ heals row 0 and fails row 2, still costing 222. Adding Z4Z_4Z4​ removes the final flag. The completed Z0Z2Z4Z_0Z_2Z_4Z0​Z2​Z4​ is logical: it commutes with all checks but anticommutes with the logical X0X1X_0X_1X0​X1​.

Panel d instead uses cyclic inputs with L=3L=3L=3. Its dictionary is VV(j,y)↦h(j−1,y)\mathrm{VV}(j,y)\mapsto h(j-1,y)VV(j,y)↦h(j−1,y), CC(x,y)↦v(x,y)\mathrm{CC}(x,y)\mapsto v(x,y)CC(x,y)↦v(x,y), X(x,y)↦A(x,y)X(x,y)\mapsto A(x,y)X(x,y)↦A(x,y), and Z(j,y)↦B(j−1,y)Z(j,y)\mapsto B(j-1,y)Z(j,y)↦B(j−1,y), with indices modulo LLL. This gives the toric code in the established edge convention.

For mmm written checks, Hproj=(Hcode+mI)/2H_{\rm proj}=(H_{\rm code}+mI)/2Hproj​=(Hcode​+mI)/2. A satisfied term contributes (1−1)/2=0(1-1)/2=0(1−1)/2=0; a failed term contributes (1+1)/2=1(1+1)/2=1(1+1)/2=1. This rescales the course's excitation cost of two.

Low energy concentrates most X- and Z-basis outcomes in sets with few violated constraints. The cited family's expansion property separates each set into distant Hamming clusters, whose strings differ at many positions. A quantum state cannot concentrate in one cluster in both conjugate bases. At least one outcome distribution must therefore spread appreciable weight across separated clusters.

A shallow bounded-arity unitary circuit from a product state cannot create that required spread across macroscopically separated clusters. The source turns this mechanism into the stated bound NLTS Hamiltonians from good quantum codes, PDF pp. 2–3 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1145/3564246.3585114. Here Ω(log⁡n)\Omega(\log n)Ω(logn) means at least a positive constant times log⁡n\log nlogn for sufficiently large nnn. The picture motivates the obstruction; it does not prove the theorem.

Each failure costs two: 2×3=62\times3=62×3=6 and 2×5=102\times5=102×5=10. The energy sequence is 0,6,8,10,8,10,8,6,00,6,8,10,8,10,8,6,00,6,8,10,8,10,8,6,0. Its peak ten gives an upper bound.

For a lower bound, follow the raw number of flipped spins. Every flip changes weight by one, even when undoing an earlier move. Reaching weight eight from zero therefore requires visiting weight three. The supplied table says every weight-three support fails at least five checks. Every route must reach energy at least ten.

The matching bounds prove barrier ten, including routes with backtracking. The dispersed route's peak twenty-four is the cost of that chosen route, not the minimum over routes. The proof protects a classical bit against the specified flips on this finite graph; it says nothing about phase errors.

Explain three different kinds of protection

Use the L=4L=4L=4 toric route, the cube model, and the one-round record example to examine these claims:

  1. A ground-space gap gives indefinite thermal storage.
  2. A growing classical bit-flip barrier protects an arbitrary qubit.
  3. One-shot correction means no future correction is necessary.

Write one paragraph repairing each claim. State the relevant model and the additional property needed.

Hint

Ask whether the claim concerns states, error paths, or noisy observations.

Hint

For the cube, test a single Z; for a noisy round, ask what residual noise is permitted.

Check against the rubric
  • Uses the actual route and cube phase error as counterexamples.
  • States the residual-noise promise without promising perfect reports or indefinite storage.
Show model solution

On the L=4L=4L=4 torus, a Z error creates two star defects costing four. Extending its string moves the endpoints without raising that energy, and closing a winding string leaves logical action. Thus the ground-space gap alone does not establish indefinite thermal storage. A lifetime claim needs a stated bath and size-scaling analysis.

The cube Hamiltonian contains only ZZ checks. A single Z0Z_0Z0​ commutes with every check and costs zero energy, yet changes the relative phase between the all-zero and all-one states. A barrier against bit flips therefore leaves quantum phase information unprotected. An arbitrary qubit requires protection of both complementary error sectors under the specified dynamics.

Single-shot correction controls the residual error after one noisy measurement round and processing. It need not reconstruct a perfect report or remove every data error. Ongoing noise can require further rounds. The guarantee needs stated data-noise and report-noise assumptions. Good rate and distance alone imply none of these three protection claims.

Record 101010101010 makes stars at vertices 0 and 2 negative. The link v(0,0)v(0,0)v(0,0), edge 4, joins precisely those vertices. Its Z reverses both negative stars, making all four positive. Commutation with Z faces leaves all four faces positive.

Z corrections preserve the logical Z signs +1,+1+1,+1+1,+1. This prepares the selected state, without encoding arbitrary input. This record has probability 1/81/81/8.

Break the monitoring analogy

Take a hybrid circuit whose prescribed measurements are recorded. Now erase the record, and separately imagine additional unrecorded Pauli faults. Explain why the trajectory phase sketch cannot by itself predict a fault-tolerant memory threshold in either modified experiment.

Hint

Use the Bell-pair comparison for the discarded-record case.

Hint

Ask what relations would reveal the additional unknown faults.

Check against the rubric
  • Explains both modifications without treating local mixed-state entropy as entanglement.
  • Names the missing error-detection and recovery ingredients.
Show model solution

Erasing the record averages the conditional states. Each recorded Bell branch is a product state with zero entanglement. After discarding the outcome, the local entropy is ln⁡2\ln2ln2 because the branch is unknown. It cannot be substituted for the trajectory entanglement in the phase sketch.

Additional unrecorded Pauli faults change the experiment even with prescribed outcomes available. Correcting them requires relations among outcomes that reveal their effects, together with a recovery procedure and a guarantee under the stated fault model. A volume-law trajectory alone supplies neither identifiable fault evidence nor successful recovery.

The structured Floquet schedule and generic monitored dynamics therefore need separate noise analyses. Module 9 develops quantitative decoding models; this sketch supplies no numerical memory threshold.
